text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night’s KMS rotation we started getting AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt from the data-processing lambda that assumes a cross-account role. From the app logs:

maria: ```
2026-03-19T09:14:02Z ERROR Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/ci-data-role/session-2026 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777666:key/abcd-ef12-3456
	status code: 400, request id: 0a1b2c3d-4e5f
```

raj: Can you paste the KMS key policy and the trust policy for the role? Also confirm whether the lambda is calling KMS directly (GenerateDataKey/Decrypt) or via another service (SecretsManager/SSM).

maria: Lambda (account 111222333444) assumes role ci-data-role to operate on encrypted blobs stored in account 999888777666. Our library uses envelope encryption and calls KMS directly (GenerateDataKey / Decrypt).

maria: Key policy on the key (redacted):

maria: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Id": "key-default-1",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAdmin",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::999888777666:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowServiceRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/some-service-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

maria: Trust policy for the role we assume (in account 999... actually shows allowing account 111... to assume):

maria: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:root"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```

alex: Two quick calls out:
- The KMS key policy only references principals from account 999...; the actual caller is an assumed-role principal from account 111... (arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/ci-data-role/session-2026). KMS key policies must explicitly allow the IAM role (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-data-role) or the account principal.
- Ensure there are no aws:SourceAccount or kms:ViaService conditions that could block the session context. Those often trip cross-account assume-role callers.

raj: Also confirm the IAM policy attached to ci-data-role allows kms:Decrypt on the key ARN. KMS enforces both the caller IAM policy and the key policy (key policy is authoritative).

maria: The role's inline policy allows kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777666:key/abcd-ef12-3456 (we pasted it in our ticket but redacted here). simulate-principal-policy from the account returns Allowed.

raj: Run these diagnostics if you haven't already:
- aws sts get-caller-identity (from the lambda execution environment)
- aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-data-role --action-names kms:Decrypt --resource-arns arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777666:key/abcd-ef12-3456
- in key account: aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef12-3456

maria: I ran get-caller-identity and it showed the assumed-role session principal. simulate-principal-policy returned Allowed. list-grants returned an empty list.

alex: That points at the key policy. Did you add the role ARN to the key policy? Note: you must specify the role's IAM ARN (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-data-role) — not the assumed-role ARN. Also watch for JSON escaping if you applied the change via Terraform/CLI.

maria: I tried adding a permissive test statement like this (temporary):

maria: ```json
{
  "Sid": "temp-allow-crossacct",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-data-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

maria: After applying that the decrypt worked immediately. So the rotation didn't propagate an allow for the external role. Root cause confirmed.

raj: Good. For long-term fixes we usually recommend one of:
- Add the explicit role ARN(s) to the key policy (least privilege).
- Or allow the whole account principal (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:root) and restrict via a Condition such as "StringLike":{"aws:PrincipalArn":["arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-data-role"]} so you don't have to enumerate every future role.
- Consider creating a KMS grant from the key account to the external role if you prefer temporary programmatic access that doesn't require changing the key policy. Grants are useful for delegated operations (and get auto-revoked when you retire the grant).

alex: Also watch for org-level SCP denies or permission boundaries that can block kms:Decrypt. If simulate-principal-policy shows Allowed but the call still fails, check Service Control Policies and any explicit Deny in IAM policies.

maria: We'll add two mitigations: 1) CI job that runs simulate-principal-policy and a quick decrypt smoke test after key rotations, 2) update our runbook for cross-account keys to include the exact role ARN in the key policy or a conditional account statement.

security-bot: Config change detected: PR #5421 modified KMS key policy in prod (author: @maria). Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pull/5421 :eyes:

eng-oncall: Closing out incident: root cause = key policy missing cross-account role principal after rotation. Follow-ups: add simulate-principal-policy check to deploy pipeline, add decrypt smoke lambda, and update docs.

maria: Thanks all! Will follow up with the PR to make the key policy changes permanent and add the CI smoke tests. :thumbsup:
